facts.content: Patient has a 3-day history of diarrhea.
Patient experiences watery or loose stools approximately 5–6 times per day.
Patient initially had vomiting two times, now resolved.
Patient reports no blood in stools and no abdominal pain.
facts.source_text: No blood in stool; no abdo pain

facts.content: Patient feels dehydrated and has poor oral intake with decreased appetite.
facts.source_text: Feels dehydrated; poor PO intake; ↓ appetite

facts.content: Patient felt febrile at the onset but is now afebrile.
facts.source_text: Felt febrile at onset; afebrile now

facts.content: Patient feels weak but reports no headache or myalgias.
facts.source_text: Feels weak; no HA or myalgias

facts.content: Patient reports no known food triggers or contacts with sick individuals.
facts.source_text: No known food triggers or sick contacts

facts.content: Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient uses a "blue" inhaler as needed.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient's father had hypertension and died of bowel cancer approximately 10 years ago.
facts.source_text: Father—HTN; died of bowel ca ~10 yrs ago.

facts.content: Patient's mother has type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Patient lives alone and is a software engineer.
Patient has been off work for the past 3 days.
Patient is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.
Patient is assessed with acute gastroenteritis with symptoms of diarrhea for 3 days, resolved vomiting, and mild dehydration.
facts.source_text: Acute gastroenteritis — 3 days watery diarrhea, vomiting resolved, mild dehydration sx, no red flags (no blood, severe pain, persistent fever)

facts.content: Patient is encouraged to have generous oral fluid intake.
Patient is advised to use over-the-counter Dioralyte as directed.
Patient can take Paracetamol as needed for fever or aches.
Patient is to remain off work until diarrhea-free for 24–48 hours.
facts.source_text: Rest/work: Off work until diarrhea-free 24–48 hrs

facts.content: Patient should return for review if not improving by next week.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: If not improving by next week, return for review

facts.content: Patient advised to seek care urgently if there is worsening dehydration, bloody stools, persistent high fever, severe abdominal pain, or inability to keep fluids down.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: Seek care urgently if worsening dehydration (oliguria, dizziness), bloody stools, persistent/high fever, severe abdo pain, or inability to keep fluids down
